confirmed.statement: 197 students took part (125 female + 67 male + 5 undisclosed = 197; ages 18 to 29, M = 21.62, SD = 2.09); one who failed to adhere to the experimental instructions was excluded, leaving 196 analyzed. The form's participants quote is verbatim.

Participants were randomly assigned to human-only (n = 64), general-AI (n = 67), or regulated-AI (n = 65). These sum to 196, the analyzed N, so they are post-exclusion counts, as the form says. The form's assignment quote is verbatim.
The abstract gives N = 196 and the Table 3 note gives N = 196.

Table 4 column counts sum to 64, 67, and 65, and its percentages use these denominators. A chi-square rebuilt from its counts equals the printed chi2(10, N = 196) = 8.35, so the arm ns are people in the analysis sample.
confirmed.locator: p. 20, Table 4; p. 19, Prior Experience Using ChatGPT

confirmed.statement: Every three-group test reports F(2, 193), which fits 196 people in three arms. This includes the 3 x 2 mixed ANOVAs for originality, usefulness, and elaboration, so all 196 have scores on both tasks and there is no attrition beyond the one exclusion.
confirmed.locator: pp. 19-22, Preliminary and Main Analyses; pp. 27-28, Exploratory Analyses

confirmed.statement: Analyses of the two AI arms report t(130) and r(130), which fit 67 + 65 = 132 people. d recomputed from t with these ns matches the printed values (t = 8.28 gives d = 1.44; t = 2.69 gives d = 0.47).
confirmed.locator: pp. 23-24, ChatGPT Interactions; p. 28, Subjective Experience Interacting with ChatGPT

confirmed.statement: The counts are people, not ideas or ratings. Each participant submitted ONE best idea per task, the experts scored all (100%) of the 196 scripts, and the analyzed score is the mean of the two experts' ratings per participant. unit = participant and n_units = null are correct.
confirmed.locator: p. 15, Scoring Procedure; p. 16; Appendix A, pp. 33-35; Appendix B, p. 35

confirmed.statement: n_randomized = null at the study and arm level is a supported reading. The paper gives no count of people randomized and does not say which arm the excluded participant was in.
The paper reports one experiment with one procedure (Fig. 1 shows no per-arm counts), so nobody appears in two studies of the paper.

The paper names no other paper or report that uses these participants and does not mention the NUS thesis (Qiu 2025) listed in the search record. NUS ethics approval and a Yale-NUS Capstone grant to Qiu fit the thesis being an earlier write-up of the same experiment. The thesis page returned HTTP 403, so its N was not checked.
confirmed.locator: p. 41, Funding and Ethics Approval; whole document searched

confirmed.statement: The power analysis targeted at least 53 per condition. Each analyzed arm (64, 67, 65) exceeds 53, and the single study has 196 people analyzed, so criterion 2 holds.

summary: The PDF supports every participant count in the form: 197 students took part, one was excluded for not following instructions, and 196 people were analyzed in arms of 64, 67, and 65 (p. 8), which Table 4, a rebuilt chi-square (N = 196), and the F(2, 193) and t(130) degrees of freedom all reproduce. The counts are people with one scored solution each, the paper has one study and names no other paper that uses these participants, so the single study meets criterion 2 with 196 people analyzed.
